query: Which method can be used for phase stability, microstructure refinement, and property optimization, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Thermodynamic modeling using CALPHAD/PANDAT can be used for phase stability, microstructure refinement, and property optimization in high-entropy alloys.
generation.mechanism: Thermodynamic calculations rationalize experimental observations of phase stability
generation.predicted_outcome: Predicted B2 + BCC + FCC at 1000 °C; B2 + BCC + sigma at 600 °C
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in the accuracy of the CALPHAD/PANDAT model

falsification_experiment.design: Experimental validation of phase stability using XRD and SEM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the experimental results do not match the predicted phase stability, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoFeNi high entropy alloy. Intervention: Annealing at 1000 °C for 15 h. Processing: Arc melting of elemental pellets, followed by annealing at 1000 °C for 15 h under argon and water quenching. Test conditions: 1000 °C, 15 h, argon atmosphere. Structure change: Single ordered B2 phase with homogeneous elemental distribution; no phase separation observed. Property change: Saturation magnetization (Ms) = 111.6 emu/g; Coercivity (Hc) = 4.3 Oe; Microhardness = 406 VHN. Mechanism: High temperature stabilizes the single B2 phase; lack of phase separation leads to lower hardness and higher magnetization. Evidence: measured. Quote: "The samples exhibited a polycrystalline microstructure consisting of large grains."

Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoFeNi alloy. Intervention: Thermodynamic modeling (CALPHAD/PANDAT). Processing: Computational simulation using PanHEA database. Test conditions: Predicted phase stability for AlCoFeNi at 1000 °C and 600 °C. Structure change: Predicted B2 + FCC at 1000 °C; B2 + BCC at 600 °C. Property change: Not stated (model predicts phase stability). Mechanism: Thermodynamic calculations rationalize experimental observations of phase stability. Evidence: calculated. Quote: "The experimentally observed microstructures and the implied phase stability were validated by thermodynamic calculations using the CALPHAD approach within the framework of the PANDAT software."

Intervention effect. Base system: AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi alloy. Intervention: Thermodynamic modeling (CALPHAD/PANDAT). Processing: Computational simulation using PanHEA database. Test conditions: Predicted phase stability for AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi at 1000 °C and 600 °C. Structure change: Predicted B2 + BCC + FCC at 1000 °C; B2 + BCC + sigma at 600 °C. Property change: Not stated (model predicts phase stability). Mechanism: Positive enthalpy of mixing for Fe-Cr, Co-Cr, Ni-Cr systems drives phase separation. Evidence: calculated. Quote: "On the other hand, in the case of the AlCr0.5Co0.5FeNi alloy, which lies at the center of the isopleth, the equilibrium phases at 1000 °C are the B2, BCC and FCC phases while at 600 °C the equilibrium phases are the B2, BCC and sigma phases."
